mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the monetary policy stance becomes more accommodative.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 8.5% signals a weak labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic weakness becomes priced in.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales (HOUST and RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as economic growth concerns intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During an early expansion phase of the business cycle, a rising industrial production index (INDPRO) signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO rises during an early expansion phase, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening consumer confidence and residential investment, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST trends upward, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations by increasing the cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during a monetary tightening cycle when FEDFUNDS rises, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
